# v2.66 Release Notes

This stable release rolls up dev pre-release **v2.66-dev**. It adds a master
on/off switch for the read-only public API.

## ⚠️ Action required: the public API is switched off by this update

This release adds a master on/off switch for the read-only public API — and it
starts in the **off** position on every system, including ones already using the
API. **If you have anything calling `/api/public/v1`, it will stop working the
moment you update**, receiving an HTTP 503 instead of data.

To restore access, sign in as a SuperAdmin, go to **Admin › API Keys**, and click
**Enable API** in the banner at the top of the page. Your existing keys are
completely untouched — nothing needs re-issuing, and no integration needs
reconfiguring. Allow about 30 seconds for the change to take effect.

If you don't use the public API, there's nothing to do; it now stays off unless
someone deliberately turns it on.

## New: a single on/off switch for the public API

Until now, the only way to shut off external API access was to disable every key
one at a time and remember to turn them all back on later — or revoke them, which
can't be undone and forces you to issue replacements.

**Admin › API Keys** now has a status banner at the top of the page controlling the
whole API at once:

- **Green — "Public API enabled"**: keys work as normal, each still subject to its
  own status, expiry and company scope.
- **Amber — "Public API disabled"**: every request to `/api/public/v1` is refused
  with an HTTP 503, no matter how a key is configured. A key still showing
  **Active** in the table below cannot be used while the API is off.

Because the switch is separate from your keys, it works as a genuine kill switch:
turn the API off during an incident or a maintenance window, and turn it back on
to restore every integration exactly as it was.

Disabling asks for a quick confirmation first, so it can't be clicked by accident.
Enabling is a single click. Either way the change takes up to 30 seconds to reach
running requests.

The switch is **SuperAdmin-only**, like the rest of the API Keys page.

## Notes

- **This release includes a database migration** — the usual update process applies
  it for you. It adds one column to the system settings table, defaulting the API
  to disabled.
- No configuration or environment-variable changes.
- Restoring a backup never silently switches the API on; the setting stays as you
  left it on the system you're restoring to.
